$comment: Provenance for every pair in coordinates.json. A coordinate with no
source is indistinguishable from a guess six months later, and this
dataset's posture is that 'we checked' must be checkable.
'legacy-production' marks the nine that were moved from engagedmoon's
own copy on 2026-08-07. They were live and computing correct sunset
windows, but the URL they were originally read from was not recorded.
Re-source them opportunistically; do not delete them.
BATCH 1 (2026-08-07). Two source shapes below:
1. A GNIS search URL (edits.nationalmap.gov/apps/gaz-domestic) — the pair
was read from the USGS Geographic Names Information System's own
public API for that exact named feature (gaz_id noted inline). This
is the strongest tier: a federal authority publishing a coordinate
for the specific summit/lake/falls/cape, not a park or a city.
2. A specific page URL (nps.gov, stateparks.utah.gov, the town/city's
own park page, or — where GNIS does not catalogue the feature, which
is common for constructed urban parks, gardens and buildings — a
Wikipedia infobox value cross-checked against the managing
authority's own stated street address for that exact site).
3. ONE ENTRY ONLY — hilton-head-sc-coligny-beach-park — cites a source
that is neither. Read its note before copying the pattern: no
authority publishes a coordinate for that park, and the number comes
from a nonprofit photography project. It is labelled as the weakest
tier in the file so it cannot be mistaken for shapes 1 or 2.
SKIPPED — no defensible published coordinate for the NAMED viewpoint was
found (checked GNIS directly and the managing authority's own page; only
a city/park/neighbourhood-level coordinate or an ambiguous trailhead pin
existed, and using either would put a confident clock time on the wrong
spot):
- key-west-fl-mallory-square — not in GNIS (confirmed via direct API
query); the City of Key West does not publish a coordinate for the
plaza and no authority map does either.
- chicago-il-chicago-riverwalk — a 1.25-mile linear park with no single
named point; not in GNIS. Any one pin would be a guess at which
quarter-mile of it someone means.
- san-diego-ca-torrey-pines-razor-point — not in GNIS. The only
published coordinate found is labelled 'trailhead', and the trail is
short enough that trailhead vs. the actual overlook point is not a
safe substitution.
- san-diego-ca-sunset-cliffs-luscomb-point — not in GNIS. Only a
neighbourhood-level 'Sunset Cliffs' coordinate was found, which is a
centroid across a mile and a half of park — exactly what this file's
header says not to use.
- bozeman-mt-lake-butte-overlook — REMOVED in fix round 1 (2026-08-07).
Originally sourced to GNIS gaz_id 1590460, but that record's feature
class is 'Summit': it is GNIS's entry for Lake Butte the mountain, not
'Lake Butte Overlook', the constructed roadside pullout on its slope
that the row actually names — a different point roughly 1km away.
GNIS does not separately catalogue the overlook. The only coordinate
found specific to the overlook itself (44.5101, -110.2748, via
Natural Atlas, a third-party recreation site built on OSM data) is
not an authority source and could not be corroborated against one —
NPS's own 'Lake Butte Overlook Vault Toilet' place page exists
(confirming NPS treats the overlook as a distinct asset from the
summit) but does not publish coordinates in its static page content,
and a search of nearby USGS survey benchmarks turned up points on the
butte itself (~3.6km off) and at an unrelated highway pullout, not at
the overlook. Rather than use the single non-authority number, it was
removed.
- park-city-ut-jordanelle-hailstone — REMOVED in fix round 2 (2026-08-07).
The recorded source said the Utah State Parks Jordanelle directions page
'states GPS coordinates for the Hailstone Recreation Area directly'. It
does not, and re-reading it is what caught this: the page publishes four
Google Maps short links and a weather-widget lat/lng, and nothing else
numeric. The widget value (40.6170130, -111.4215710) is ~490 m from the
pair that shipped, so it is not even the number that was recorded.
The pair itself (40.6214, -111.4210) traces to recreation.gov/gateways/
coordinate for JORDANELLE STATE PARK AS A WHOLE. The row is named
'Hailstone Overlook, Jordanelle State Park', so this is the same
containing-area-substituted-for-the-named-point mistake as Lake Butte,
with a false provenance record on top of it.
A nationwide GNIS sweep for '%Hailstone%' across all ten layers returns
no overlook anywhere in the United States; the only Utah match (gaz_id
1437577) is a Populated Place — the townsite Jordanelle Reservoir
drowned in 1995 — 1.5 km away. No Utah State Parks, USGS, UGRC or
Reclamation source publishes a coordinate for a named 'Hailstone
Overlook'; no source of any kind was found containing the phrase. The
row's name, its coordinate and its cited source were three different
places, so it was removed rather than re-pointed at the park centroid.
These six keep rendering 'late afternoon', which is honest.
WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT TELL YOU, and the review both removals came from.
Every entry below is a URL, and the test in proposal-spots-data.test.ts
now enforces that it is one. That test cannot open the page. Both removals
above were pairs that PASSED every automated check in this repo: a real
URL, a real page, a well-formed coordinate inside the right state. What
found them was a person opening the cited page and reading it.
So: when you add a pair, quote the page's own coordinate text in the note,
verbatim. If you cannot quote it, the page is not the source, and saying it
is — which is what the Jordanelle entry did — is worse than recording no
source at all, because it survives review.

explanation of the sourcing method (GNIS bulk text export, not the
unreadable JS search app) and the two highlight-over-name judgement calls
(Maroon Lake, Fryxell Overlook).

coordinate, and the page's raw HTML has no embedded geo metadata

none). This is the Lake Butte mistake again: the only feature GNIS
has a coordinate for is the thing being photographed, not the
constructed overlook the row names.
- whitefish-mt-hidden-lake-overlook — same shape. GNIS has 'Hidden
Lake' itself (gaz_id 772374, Lake, Flathead County MT, 48.6758541,

County MT, 48.6866407,-113.7367819) — a mountain pass on the ridge

railing (nothing ties the two together), so it was not guessed at.
NPS's own trailhead page (nps.gov/places/hidden-lake-trailhead.htm,
the row's cited sourceUrl) states trail distance and elevation stats
but no coordinate, checked directly including raw HTML for embedded
geo metadata (none found).
- san-francisco-ca-shakespeare-garden — not in GNIS (constructed
garden). No dedicated Wikipedia article exists (confirmed by
search — only 'Shakespeare Garden (Evanston, Illinois)' has one).
SF Rec & Park's own page (sfrecpark.org/913/Golden-Gate-Park---
Shakespeare-Garden, checked directly) gives only a cross-street
description — 'Martin Luther King Drive, between Nancy Pelosi Drive
and Music Concourse Drive' — not a coordinate, and geocoding that
description would be exactly the guess this file's rules forbid.
- san-diego-ca-torrey-pines-razor-point and
san-diego-ca-sunset-cliffs-luscomb-point were already skipped in
Batch 1 (see above) and are reconfirmed, not re-derived: the same
two authority pages (parks.ca.gov and sandiego.gov) were re-checked
directly this batch and still publish no coordinate for either named
point, only general park descriptions and driving directions.
park-city-ut-jordanelle-hailstone remains untouched — already adjudicated
unsourceable in Batch 1, not re-derived (see above and the task brief).
SOURCED this batch, all via the GNIS bulk text export
(https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/GeographicNames/
DomesticNames/DomesticNames_<ST>_Text.zip) unless noted otherwise. Each
note quotes the exact pipe-delimited row read (gaz_id|feature_name|
feature_class|state_name|...|county_name|...|prim_lat_dec|prim_long_dec
at the tail, trimmed to the relevant fields).

REVIEW FIXES (2026-08-07): two more Group B entries removed after a
review found their sourcing broken. Full reasoning in coordinates.json's
$comment; short version here:
- bend-or-watchman-overlook — the cited NPS asset's coordinate was a
2009 photo's geotag (the scene photographed), not the standpoint. USGS
elevation lookup confirms the point sits on Crater Lake's own surface
(1,880.5 m, against the lake's published 1,883 m), ~3.4 km from the
real overlook. Removed, not re-pointed at a guessed rim value.
- seattle-wa-deception-pass-bridge — the cited Wikipedia infobox quote
does not exist and never has: the article's raw wikitext currently
carries no coordinate (none since 25 Nov 2022), and no revision in its
history ever held the value this entry quoted. No replacement
authority source was found (GNIS has no Bridge feature class or record
for it; WSDOT's page 404s; NBI has no reachable public endpoint).
Removed rather than kept with an unverifiable note.
